We looked and could not find reliable evidence. We say so plainly instead of guessing. When the answer waits on someone in the seat, mark it Explicit Unknown (in-seat).

✦ Tell me more · explain this simply
These are the six statements the team can say out loud today without overclaiming. Each carries a confidence level. The short version: Band C is real and growing; buyers care most about ease and a human who answers; MB's edge is finance (gifts flow into the books in one vendor) but that is a closing argument, not an opener; nobody in the market proves outcomes; MB cannot yet show a safe switch; and there are no public reviews of today's Amplify product.

Story order

Open: ease + human support → Middle: one place / time back (Conditional until R2) → Close: gift-to-books for the finance lead → Hygiene only: fees. Never open on fees or giving growth.

Discovery ask, not Amplify claim: ease + support opens as buyer language (CM2), not a proven Amplify claim until R3 clears.

The order of the sales conversation. Start with what buyers say they want (easy, someone answers). Then 'one place' (only once proven). Finish with gift-to-books for the finance person. Fees are housekeeping, never the headline.

  • Open with discovery, not a claim: ask about ease and support pain in their words.
  • Demo only the pains they named. Refuse theater and giving-lift stats.

  1. Channel order: warm intro / judicatory first, then researched contract-window outbound. Conferences and megachurch theater are not Core pipeline.
  2. Size-gate every MQL (250–999) before the dial.
  3. Conversation order is locked: ease + support → one place → gift-to-books; fees are hygiene. The open is CM2 buyer language, not Amplify proof while R3 is Unknown.
